In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Devanagari is a syllabary with a twist, and that the twist is morphological.
the alphasyllabaries are a neglected case in the literature on reading.

the orthographic system is a complex and dynamic system that is influenced by the morphological, phonological, and semantic properties of words, and that the orthographic processing of words is a dynamic and flexible system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Devanagari script, like other syllabic scripts, has a complex structure, which needs to be taken into account while modeling orthographic processing.
the Devanagari script, despite being an alphasyllabaries, does not allow a simple position-based encoding of characters, and that the encoding of character position is constrained by morphology.
the Devanagari writing system is a hybrid of an alphasyllabaries and alphabets, and that its orthography is best described in terms of both the position and the morpheme status of the akṣara.
The main takeaway from our work is that
orthography is not a universal phenomenon and hence models of reading must be sensitive to orthographic variation across languages.
a model of orthographic processing must be sensitive to both the morphological and orthographic properties of the script.

a model of word recognition must be sensitive to the morphological structure, and the nature of morphological structure (i.e. whether it is agglutinative or non-agglutinative) should also be factored in while developing models of orthographic processing.
